**L. Granda, P.J. Moya-Fernández, R.M. Soriano-Miras and F. González-Gómez** (*Sustainable Water Resources Management*, 2024). [Read the article](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40899-023-01027-6).

**The question.** Do women and men save water at home in the same way?

**What they found.**

- There is no gender gap in the number of water-saving habits.
- But there are differences in specific habits.
- They follow how household chores are shared: tasks traditionally done by women or by men.

**Key result (in the video).** Saving water at home: women and men. *Source: Sustainable Water Resources Management (2024), ten household water uses.*

**Why it matters.** Water-saving campaigns work better when they reach the person who actually does each household task.

**Link with inequality.** Gender inequality in sharing household chores also shapes who carries the effort of saving water at home.
